title: Console walkthrough — Usage signals & per-route cost (AetherWorks)
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked AetherWorks through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost decomposition. Focus on mapping routes to chargeback tags, exploring route-level latency/cost tradeoffs, and security considerations for Private deployments. Customer requested sandbox access, security package, and an initial POC to validate per-route billing with their tagging scheme.
next_steps: Samir to provision console sandbox (read-only) and send link by 2026-02-28
Hannah to share POC benchmark checklist and model recommendations by 2026-03-03
Redwood to send SOC 2 + security pack and network/ports doc
Schedule a 60-min POC kickoff the week of 2026-03-08
action_items: Hannah - POC checklist & suggested model/quantization configs (due 2026-03-03)
Samir - share billing mapping template and example CSV (due 2026-03-01)
Carlos - send sample route tagging schema and top 10 routes (due 2026-03-02)
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samir (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see Carlos, Priya and Eliot on the call - hi, good to see you. We'll run through the Console — usage signals, per-route dashboards, and then walk into cost decomposition. Hannah will jump into the deep telemetry slides and the sandbox.
[00:00:32] Carlos (AetherWorks): Hi Samir. Thanks. We're excited — we've been trying to get a handle on per-route spend. Our finance team is asking for chargeback by product line.
[00:00:45] Priya (AetherWorks): Yeah, hi. We want to understand how Redwood maps API routes to costs and how we can tag stuff from our side, also SLOs.
[00:00:55] Hannah (Redwood SE): Great, we'll start with the usage lens. Quick note: I'll be a little screen-share heavy. If anything's fuzzy on the transcript you'll have the recording + the deck link later.
[00:01:10] Eliot (AetherWorks FinOps): Also curious about rate-limits, reserved capacity and can we see historical chargebacks — last quarter spikes were weird.
[00:01:22] Samir: Perfect, let's go. (screen-share) Alright, Console home. Top-level is the Usage Overview — tokens, requests, average latency across models. We surfaced anomalies automatically — see the red bar here is a spike in long-context generation on Feb 10th. That's often a KV cache miss pattern.
[00:01:48] Priya: When you say KV cache miss, do you mean our sessions lost their context? We saw user sessions with 10x tokens that day.
[00:01:56] Hannah: Exactly — the KV cache metric shows a drop in prefix hits. Sometimes clients rotate keys or use new model variants and that invalidates cached prefixes. We surface a 'cache-hit ratio' per route so you can correlate cost increases.
[00:02:16] Carlos: Ok, where would that show up in the per-route dashboards?
[00:02:20] Hannah: Navigate to Routes -> Per-route telemetry. (click) Here you pick a route — e.g. /chat/assistant — and you get token counts, median latency, p95 latency, and cost per 1k tokens. Notice the small sparkline under 'cache-hit ratio'. You can overlay costs and latency.
[00:02:45] Samir: I'll point out that you can tag routes with your product team name or chargeback tag. Those tags get pushed into the billing export so your finance team can pivot on them.
[00:02:58] Eliot: Is the tag something we set on our side or through Redwood? We want it tied to our internal SKU.
[00:03:04] Hannah: Both. You can supply tags in the API request header or set them in the Console mapping layer if you want to translate Redwood's route name to your internal SKUs. We also accept an outbound mapping CSV to reconcile names.
[00:03:19] Priya: Good. How granular is the cost breakdown? Can we see per-model, per-batch, and per-caller-id?
[00:03:26] Hannah: Yep. Cost is decomposed to model variant, route, and caller-id. We show an estimated per-token compute cost and add network and storage where applicable. Important caveat — hosted includes underlying model variant pricing; with Dedicated you get predictable slot-based economics.
[00:03:46] Carlos: Speaking of Dedicated vs Hosted, our security team prefers private deployment but finance likes hosted for variable cost. Any way to route low-latency, fin-heavy workloads to Dedicated and keep bursty stuff hosted?
[00:03:59] Samir: Absolutely — smart routing policy. You can set a policy that pins certain callers/routes to Dedicated capacity, while fallback goes to hosted or a cheaper quantized variant. We helped a customer reduce tail costs by routing non-sensitive inference to quantized variants.
[00:04:20] Eliot: OK, show me the chargeback CSV.
[00:04:24] Hannah: (navigates) Under Billing -> Export, here's the CSV sample. It includes columns: timestamp, route, tags, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, compute_estimate_usd, storage_estimate_usd, total_estimate_usd. You can ingest that to your chargeback pipeline.
[00:04:45] Priya: So compute_estimate_usd — is that based on your per-GPU kernel selection or an average unit price?
[00:04:53] Hannah: It's based on our runtime cost model — kernel selection, observed sequence length distribution, and batch efficiency. It's a model-informed estimate. We also let you override with your own unit costs if you're on Dedicated.
[00:05:07] Carlos: How accurate is it month over month? The spike earlier in Feb threw our numbers off by 22%.
[00:05:14] Samir: Spikes can come from mis-tagging or cache misses. Our accuracy improves when you pass us caller-id and route tags. For marketplace customers we see +/- 5-7% when tagging is consistent.
[00:05:28] Eliot: What about SSO and who can see chargeback data? We need RBAC — finance shouldn't be able to change routing.
[00:05:35] Hannah: Console RBAC supports granular roles. You can make a 'Billing Viewer' that sees billing exports and dashboards but cannot edit routes or routing policies. SAML SSO is supported; we sync group membership and map it to RBAC.
[00:05:50] Priya: And audit logs? We need immutable logs for compliance.
[00:05:54] Samir: We keep an append-only audit trail with who changed a route, timestamp, and before/after. If you want, we can stream logs to your SIEM or S3 for retention policies.
[00:06:07] Carlos: KMS — where are keys kept for Private?
[00:06:10] Hannah: For Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM. Keys are never seen by Redwood; we use envelope encryption. For hosted we offer our managed KMS but customers with high compliance choose to bring their own.
[00:06:23] Eliot: Great. Now, on the Optimize side, you mentioned batching and quantization suggestions — can you show an example where batching improves cost without killing latency?
[00:06:31] Hannah: Sure. (switches tab) Here's the Optimize panel. It ingests your latency SLOs and usage patterns, then suggests batching targets per route. For conversational UI with short requests we recommend smaller batch windows (10–20ms). For embeddings or bulk rerank we recommend larger batch windows to increase throughput.
[00:06:51] Priya: Is there an automatic policy we can enable or is this manual?
[00:06:55] Hannah: Both. You can use 'Auto-Batch' with constraints (max latency overhead, max tokens per batch). It adapts to incoming QPS. We surfaced per-route recommendations after analyzing your last 30 days of traffic.
[00:07:10] Carlos: Can Optimize recommend quantization levels? Our human-in-the-loop models are sensitive to quality.
[00:07:15] Hannah: Yes — it ranks candidate quant levels against your eval set. We run a micro-eval and show expected degradation metrics. Typically for NLU tasks 8-bit quant works; for generation with long context you may want 16-bit. We provide suggested rollouts: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on quality regressions.
[00:07:36] Eliot: That rollback is crucial. How do you detect regressions? We have a prompt-set we evaluate against.
[00:07:41] Samir: You can upload eval prompt sets into Console. Redwood's eval runner runs A/B tests and flags BLEU-like deltas and hallucination rate increases. We tie alerts to your rollouts and can auto-fallback to previous variant.
[00:07:58] Priya: Walk me through a real chargeback example — route to finance.
[00:08:02] Hannah: Ok. Example: Route '/image-caption' had 120k tokens in Feb; model = rdx-3b-quant; tokens_in/out and compute estimate produced $730 for compute, $45 for storage. We apply tag 'product:mobile-app' and export that row. Finance sees mobile-app = $12k month. If you switch to a larger batch size and quantized model, estimate drops to $520 compute.
[00:08:30] Carlos: Can we set alerts if a route cost exceeds a threshold?
[00:08:33] Hannah: Yes — Alerts -> Cost -> New alert. You can set daily or rolling 7-day thresholds and get slack/email/pagerduty notifications. We also provide anomaly detection automatically.
[00:08:44] Eliot: The anomaly detection yesterday flagged more errors, but we didn't know which route. Can you narrow down anomalous latency to a specific caller-id?
[00:08:51] Hannah: Absolutely — from the anomaly card click 'Investigate' and choose dimension 'caller-id' or 'route'. It will show the top N contributors to the spike and let you open raw request traces.
[00:09:06] Priya: Nice. How deep are the traces? Do we get token-level timings?
[00:09:10] Hannah: We capture stage timings: request deserialize, model compute, streaming time. We don't record token-by-token timings by default for PII reasons, but you can enable verbose traces for a narrow window.
[00:09:24] Carlos: Ok. A couple of security questions — we need SOC 2 and ISO docs, and a pen test report. Do you provide those?
[00:09:31] Samir: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO attestation. For pen test, we can share our recent third-party summary and coordinate an enterprise pen test if necessary for Private.
[00:09:44] Eliot: Great. For the POC, we want to test per-route billing accuracy and Optimize recommendations — can you give us a simple checklist?
[00:09:52] Hannah: We'll send a one-page POC checklist but high-level: 1) Provide top 10 routes + sample payloads, 2) add caller-id and tags to requests (or tell us mapping), 3) choose two target models (hosted + quantized), 4) set evaluation prompt set, 5) run workload for 48–72 hours and we'll capture telemetry and provide a report.
[00:10:14] Carlos: That works. We usually run in our staging first. Will the sandbox show representative costs?
[00:10:19] Hannah: The sandbox is read-only with historical telemetry from a small demo dataset. For live costing we'll provision a trial key for a 2-week test with billing estimates. That's one of Samir's action items.
[00:10:33] Samir: I'll take care of the sandbox and the trial key. We'll also attach the billing template CSV and a short video showing tag setup.
[00:10:41] Priya: Awesome. Can we see an example route mapping config? I want to know how flexible the route transforms are.
[00:10:47] Hannah: Sure. (scrolls) Here's a transform rule: match regex on path, extract product id, map to tag product:mobile-app or product:web. You can also rewrite model selection by route (e.g. /batch -> rdx-3b-quant) and set routing policy.
[00:11:05] Carlos: Any gotchas on long context? Our chat product uses 8k windows.
[00:11:09] Hannah: For long-context, the runtime chooses different kernels and cache strategies. We recommend pinning long-context routes to Dedicated when possible because cost predictability and KV cache residency are better with Dedicated.
[00:11:23] Eliot: And if we can't get Dedicated across the board, is there a mixed approach?
[00:11:27] Samir: Yes — route-level policy. You can set 'sensitive:false' to route to hosted quantized variant, 'sensitive:true' to private/dedicated. The Console will show an availability and estimated latency per region so you can plan.
[00:11:44] Priya: How about retention on logs — our security wants 1 year of request logs.
[00:11:48] Hannah: We support configurable retention when you're on Enterprise retention add-on. For hosted default is 90 days, but we can extend and stream to your S3.
[00:11:58] Carlos: Great. This is useful. A few quick clarifications: 1) can we see an example of a chargeback sheet for a single week? 2) how do we reconcile usage with our internal metrics?
[00:12:09] Hannah: For (1) — yes, the weekly export has daily rows; we'll share an example. For (2) — include caller-id in your client and match that to your internal user_id; we provide a reconciliation guide.
[00:12:22] Eliot: Anything about network egress costs? We have multi-region users.
[00:12:26] Samir: Network egress can be included in the estimate if you enable network metering. For Private, if you deploy in your region egress is within your VPC. For hosted, we attribute egress costs to the route in the billing export.
[00:12:39] Priya: Show me again where alerts live.
[00:12:42] Hannah: Alerts -> Create -> Cost anomaly. Example: threshold > $500/day for route '/search/relevance'. We can also toggle 'notify on anomaly' which uses profiling to detect unusual per-token increases.
[00:12:58] Carlos: I'm seeing a section called 'Workloads' — what is that?
[00:13:01] Hannah: Workloads groups routes into logical sets. E.g., 'mobile chat' includes /chat/* routes and inherits default batching/quantization. It's great for product-level views.
[00:13:13] Priya: Can we import our own workload definitions via API?
[00:13:16] Hannah: Yes — the Workloads API accepts a JSON mapping and you can bind models and policies programmatically.
[00:13:25] (slightly overlapping) Carlos: Hmm, the console shows p95 increases at 14:00 on Tuesday — can we jump into traces for that?
[00:13:31] Hannah: Click Investigate -> traces. Here's a trace sample: request id, caller-id, route, time breakdown. (reads) This one shows a serialization bump due to large metadata in payloads — that was something a customer fixed by compressing metadata.
[00:13:52] Eliot: Compression — do you support gzip on request bodies?
[00:13:55] Hannah: Yes, compressed payloads are supported, and we surface decompressed payload size in telemetry.
[00:14:02] Priya: Anything we need to change client-side for better batching?
[00:14:06] Hannah: Send batched payloads where semantically possible, include caller-id, and keep prompt lengths predictable. Avoid dynamic long-tail prompts if you want high batch efficiency.
[00:14:18] Carlos: For the POC, we will send the top 10 routes and sample payloads. Also, finance will want a weekly artifact. Can you generate a templated PDF report?
[00:14:28] Samir: Yes, we can generate a weekly POC report with top cost drivers, suggested optimizations, and expected savings. We'll include an appendix with traces and tag mapping.
[00:14:39] Priya: One more question — can we schedule a security deep dive? Our InfoSec wants network diagrams and firewall ports.
[00:14:45] Samir: Yep, we'll set that up. I'll attach the network/ports doc in the follow-up email.
[00:14:52] Eliot: Anything else on the Console itself? I like the cost breakdown but want to see the exact math.
[00:14:58] Hannah: The Export has the compute breakdown with assumptions: GPU cost per minute, average token per second, batch efficiency. We'll send the assumptions in the spreadsheet so you can adjust them to your internal costs.
[00:15:12] Carlos: Ok sounds good. Let's talk timeline — we want POC kickoff next week.
[00:15:17] Samir: We can do that. I'll send a calendar invite for a 60-min POC kickoff the week of Mar 8th after you send the route list. Action items are in the notes.
[00:15:27] (short silence) [00:26:12] Priya: sorry, audio drop — can you repeat the sandbox permissions?
[00:26:18] Samir: The sandbox is read-only for Console; the trial key will be a separate credential that allows limited write for the trial window. If you want full admin access we can provision an admin account for one user.
[00:26:32] Hannah: Also note the sandbox contains synthetic data. Live trial will collect real telemetry for the POC.
[00:26:40] Carlos: Understood.
[00:36:05] Eliot: Quick question — you mentioned auto-fallback to a simpler model if quality metrics fail. How fast is that cutover?
[00:36:12] Hannah: The fallback policy is near-instant for new requests; it switches on the routing layer. For in-flight streaming requests there may be partial responses; we recommend small canaries to validate.
[00:36:24] Priya: Ok. That's fine. Any risk of throttling with auto-batch?
[00:36:28] Hannah: Auto-batch will respect your rate-limits; there's a max latency overhead setting that prevents batch windows from causing SLO violations.
[00:36:37] Carlos: Good. I'll gather the top 10 routes and send them today. Expect an internal note from FinOps about the chargeback template.
[00:36:45] Eliot: Yep, will do.
[00:36:49] Samir: Great. To recap: Samir will provision sandbox and trial key, Hannah will send POC checklist and model suggestions, Samir will attach SOC2/ISO pack and network doc, Carlos will send route list. We'll schedule POC kickoff for week of Mar 8th. Any objections?
[00:37:05] Priya: No objections.
[00:37:07] Carlos: Sounds good.
[00:37:09] Eliot: Thanks everyone.
[00:37:11] Samir: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links. Bye.
[00:53:00] (meeting ended)
